fullDescription:
Two and a half hours paddling Klong Root, a spring-fed channel inland from Ao Nang that most visitors never hear about.

The water comes up out of the limestone, which is why it is that particular clear emerald and why it stays cool when everything on the coast is warm. You can see the bottom the whole way along. The channel is narrow with jungle closing overhead, waterlilies across the surface and vines hanging down to the waterline, and because it is freshwater and inland there is no swell, no salt and no engine noise.

The kayak is the only way through. The channel is too shallow and too narrow for anything with a motor, so the loudest thing on the water is your own paddle.

There is a swim stop halfway. Freshwater springs run cold enough to be a genuine shock after the Andaman, which is the point of stopping there rather than at the end.

Kingfishers work the channel edges and are the bird you will actually see rather than the one in the brochure; monitor lizards sun themselves on the banks.

This is the trip for a day when the sea is closed. Klong Root is inland freshwater, so wind and swell do not touch it, and from May to October it runs on days when every island boat in Ao Nang is cancelled. It is also the right choice with young children, who do not need to swim to enjoy it.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the kayak and paddle, life jacket and dry bag, an English-speaking local guide, the entrance fee, drinking water, and photos taken by your guide.

Two and a half hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Spring-fed channel, clear to the bottom and cool year-round
Kayak only: too shallow and narrow for any motor
Freshwater swim stop, genuinely cold after the sea
Runs when wind and swell cancel the island boats
Kingfishers, monitor lizards, waterlilies and hanging vines

fullDescription:
The four islands in the second half of the day, finishing with a barbecue as the light goes.

Morning boats all leave Ao Nang inside the same hour and reach each beach together. Going out at midday means arriving at the later stops as the fleet turns for home, so the last two islands of this trip are quieter than the same islands were four hours earlier.

The route is Poda, Chicken Island, Tup and Mor. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is the sandbar that links Tup and Mor as the tide drops and vanishes when it comes back, so an afternoon trip on a falling tide walks out onto sand the morning boats passed over.

Snorkelling is over shallow coral close to the beaches, forgiving enough that you do not need to be a confident swimmer.

Sunset is taken from the water with the Ao Nang karsts in front of you. Limestone holds colour a long time after the sun has gone, so the light lasts past the point the clock suggests it should.

Dinner is a barbecue rather than a packed box.

One thing to check when booking: hotel pickup depends on which option you choose. Confirm it is included in yours, or work out how you are reaching the pier, because the Ao Nang and Krabi Town piers are twenty minutes apart.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers dinner, fruit, drinking water, snorkelling equipment and life jackets, with hotel pickup and drop-off depending on the option chosen.

Six hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Midday start, arriving as the morning fleet leaves
Thale Waek sandbar on a falling tide
Shallow snorkelling that suits weak swimmers
Sunset over the Ao Nang karsts from the water
Check whether hotel pickup is in your chosen option

fullDescription:
Eight hours across the four islands with a guide working in both English and Thai, and a beginner-friendly approach to the water.

The length is what separates this from the standard circuit. Most Krabi island trips run five or six hours and keep everyone moving; at eight, the stops last long enough to swim properly, dry off and sit down.

Phra Nang Cave Beach sits under an overhanging limestone cliff on the Railay peninsula, with the shrine at one end where fishermen leave carved wooden offerings to a spirit they believe protects them at sea. It is still in use rather than preserved for visitors, which is worth knowing before photographing it.

Chicken Rock is the formation at the tip of Ko Gai, which reads as a chicken's head from one angle on the approach and as an ordinary limestone stack from everywhere else. Ko Thap and the Ao Nang tombolo are the sandbar: a strip that emerges at low tide to link islands into a walkable spit and disappears as the water returns. Whether you walk it is decided by the tide table, not the operator.

The snorkelling here is set up for beginners. Krabi's reef sits shallow and close in, so several stops are shallow enough to stand in, and the guide works with people who have not used a mask before.

A guide who speaks Thai as well as English matters more than it sounds: the boat crew are local, and the person who can talk to both them and you is the person who can change plans when the sea does.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers lunch, drinking water, seasonal fruit, hotel pickup and drop-off, an English- and Thai-speaking local guide, and beginner snorkelling support.

Eight hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Eight hours, so stops are long enough to actually swim
Phra Nang beach and its working fishermen's shrine
Sandbar walkable only when the tide allows
Snorkelling set up for people who have never used a mask
Guide works in Thai as well as English, so plans can change

fullDescription:
Phi Phi in a small group with an early Maya Bay slot and the national park fee already in the price.

Maya Bay closed completely from 2018 to 2022 so the reef could recover. It reopened under strict rules that most listings do not spell out: boats moor at the back of Phi Phi Leh and visitors walk in through the island, swimming inside the bay is restricted, and daily numbers are capped. An early slot means walking in before the queue rather than after it, which on a capped site is the whole difference.

The small-group format matters on this route specifically. Large Phi Phi boats carry forty or more and the bottleneck is not the sailing, it is the moving: queueing to disembark, queueing to re-board, snorkelling in a crowd. A smaller group clears each stop faster and spends the saved time in the water.

The 400 THB national park fee is included rather than collected at the pier. Nothing is collected at the pier, so the figure here is the whole cost of the day.

A Thai buffet lunch is included, and meeting point and drop-off cover all Ao Nang hotels.

Seven and a half hours with an early start. Phi Phi trips are open-sea crossings and a speedboat pounds in any chop; anyone prone to seasickness should take something before boarding rather than after.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Early Maya Bay slot, ahead of the queue on a capped site
Post-2022 rules: walk in, restricted swimming, daily cap
Small group, so less queueing at every stop
400 THB national park fee in the price, not at the pier
Meeting point and drop-off for all Ao Nang hotels

fullDescription:
Ninety minutes feeding elephants at a sanctuary reached by boat from Ao Nam Mao pier.

The transfer is part of what makes it. The sanctuary sits away from the Ao Nang strip, and the crossing from Ao Nam Mao is what keeps it out in the quiet rather than beside the tourist road.

You prepare the food and hand it over yourself. Elephant feed here is bananas, sugarcane and rice-and-tamarind balls rolled by hand, and an adult Asian elephant puts away something like 150 kilograms of plant matter a day, which reorders your sense of what keeping one involves. The rest of the time is spent close to the animals while they do ordinary elephant things.

No riding, no chains during the programme, no performances. The elephants here came out of logging and trekking work, and the keepers who look after them daily run the session.

Ninety minutes is a comfortable length for this. You stay dry, you do not need a change of clothes, and it works with children who would lose interest in a half-day programme.

Snacks, seasonal fruit, juice, coffee, tea and drinking water are served, and the elephant food is provided, so there is nothing to buy on site.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers a tour guide, all refreshments, food to feed the elephants, and the return transfer to Ao Nam Mao pier.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Reached by boat from Ao Nam Mao, away from the Ao Nang strip
Prepare the food by hand, then feed it yourself
No riding, no chains, no performances
Run by the keepers who look after the animals daily
Stay dry, no change of clothes needed, works with children

fullDescription:
Half an hour making elephant food by hand and feeding it to the herd.

You roll the food before you hand it over: bananas, sugarcane and rice-and-tamarind balls. An adult Asian elephant eats in the region of 150 kilograms of plant matter a day, and making a few kilos of it yourself is the fastest way to understand what that actually means.

No riding, no chains during the programme, no performances. The animals came out of logging and riding work and now live on the land the sanctuary keeps for them.

Thirty minutes on dry ground suits a lot of people better than a longer programme does. Nobody gets wet, nothing needs a change of clothes, and small children get close to an elephant for exactly as long as they can hold their attention. It also slots either side of a boat trip without taking the day.

The sanctuary sits inland from the coast, on land kept for the herd rather than a roadside pen, so the drive out is short but takes you properly out of the resort strip.

Hotel transfer from Ao Nang, Klong Muang and Nopparat Thara is included, along with every ingredient and material you will use, plus coffee, tea, drinking water and seasonal fruit.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Roll the food by hand, then feed it to the herd
No riding, no chains, no performances
Stay dry, on dry ground, no change of clothes
Short enough for small children and easy to fit around a boat trip
Hotel transfer from Ao Nang, Klong Muang and Nopparat Thara
